{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel to Customer)  
**Re:** Review of Master Services Agreement — playbook findings and recommended positions

---

## Executive Summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The commercial core of the agreement is strong: indemnification (§ 20), IP and data ownership (§ 14), limitation of liability (§ 21), licence grant (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), governing law (§ 28), warranties (§ 19), transition assistance (§ 11), insurance (§ 18), and the absence of minimum purchase commitments (§ 2.1) all meet or exceed our preferred positions and require no redline.

Seven issues require negotiation. Three of them sit at our walk-away positions and must be resolved before signature: the full-term exclusivity binding us as Customer (§ 2.2, which also drives the non-compete finding), the Customer-side most-favoured-nation obligation (§ 7.2), and Vendor's unlimited, no-notice audit right with remote access to our systems (§ 22.1). In addition, § 7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day in liquidated damages payable by us with no threshold or cap; § 9 contains no Customer termination-for-convenience right despite a three-year committed term; § 8.2 requires 180 days' non-renewal notice; and § 12.4 imposes a one-sided 18-month non-solicit/no-hire on us.

Notably, several of these burdens contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. That internal inconsistency supports our deletion requests as conforming edits rather than commercial concessions.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Title | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN | Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 |
| Critical | IP | Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 |
| Critical | LOL-CAP | Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 |
| High | LD | Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 |
| High | T4C | Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9 (Termination) |
| High | ASSIGN | Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 |
| High | LICENSE | Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 |
| Medium | AUDIT | Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 |
| Medium | MFN | Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT | Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 |
| Medium | RENEWAL | Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | **Deviation** | § 8.2 |
| Medium | GOVLAW | Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT | Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2.1 |
| Medium | TRANSITION | Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 |
| Medium | WARRANTY | Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 |
| Low | INSURANCE | Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 |

---

## Walk-Away Items

These three items are identified in the playbook as walk-away positions. We should not sign without resolution.

**1. Exclusivity / non-compete — § 2.2.** Section 2.2 makes Vendor our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the entire term, with no category limit, no time limit and no performance-based exit. It also contradicts § 2.1 (no minimum quantity or purchase commitment) and § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges no exclusivity or non-compete commitment). We are deleting § 2.2; § 12.3's disclaimer then governs. *Fallback, if pressed:* a category-limited 12-month exclusivity confined to a single named competing product, with automatic termination on service-level or delivery failure and carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.

**2. Customer-side MFN — § 7.2.** Section 7.2 would require us to extend Vendor the best terms we offer any other technology supplier, with no product scope, time limit or comparison carve-outs. MFN is acceptable only in the Customer's favour. The clause also conflicts with § 12.3. No other clause depends on it and no Vendor-granted MFN is affected, so deletion is the minimal edit.

**3. Unlimited Vendor audit with remote access — § 22.1.** Section 22.1 permits Vendor to audit us at any time without notice and to remotely access our systems and records. This also contradicts § 22.2, which already bars direct system access and allocates audit cost to Vendor unless underpayment exceeds five percent. We are adding the missing guardrails — once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent confidentiality-bound auditor, off-site records review — and deleting the remote-access grant, leaving §§ 22.2 and 22.3 intact.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven deviations, with playbook comments explaining each change and the fallback where one exists:
   - Delete § 2.2 (exclusivity/non-compete binding Customer).
   - Delete § 7.2 (Customer-side MFN).
   - Delete the Customer-payable liquidated damages in § 7.6 and replace with excused-performance relief for Vendor (schedule relief plus documented out-of-pocket costs). The current USD 25,000 per day, with no materiality threshold, notice requirement or aggregate cap, can exceed contract value on minor administrative slippage.
   - Add a new § 9.4 giving Customer a termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees (leveraging the existing § 10.2 refund mechanics), and confirm Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right during a committed term. This is required because § 8.1 commits us to a three-year term with 12-month auto-renewals under § 8.2.
   - Rewrite § 22.1 per the audit guardrails above.
   - Amend § 8.2 to reduce the non-renewal notice window from 180 days to 30 days and add a Vendor renewal reminder 60 days before renewal. The 12-month renewal term and the § 8.3 uplift cap (lesser of CPI and 3%, on 90 days' notice) are already compliant and should be left alone.
   - Delete § 12.4 (Customer-only 18-month non-solicit/no-engage covering all Vendor employees). *Fallback:* mutual, 12 months, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire element.
2. **Flag the § 12.3 inconsistency to Vendor** in the cover note — §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgment in § 12.3, which should make the deletions straightforward.
3. **Confirm with the business** the acceptability of the two fallbacks (limited exclusivity; mutual 12-month non-solicit) before we concede either, and whether a Customer convenience right is a condition of signature given the three-year commitment.
4. **Order Form drafting note for the deal team:** "Deliverable" under § 14 is limited to work product an Order Form identifies as created specifically for Customer, and ownership is conditioned on payment of the applicable Fees. We should ensure each Order Form identifies the intended deliverables expressly. No amendment to the MSA is needed for this.
5. **No action required** on indemnification, IP and data ownership, limitation of liability, licence scope, assignment, governing law, minimum commitments, transition assistance, warranty or insurance — these are compliant and should be protected from erosion in any Vendor counter-redline."}
